author: NorthEast News Desk
body: American sailor Charlotte Rose won the ILCA 6 Women’s World Championship on Saturday after navigating two final races in difficult conditions on Dublin Bay. Rose carried 15 points from qualifying and finished second and sixth in the medal-deciding series to end the regatta with 23 points.

Belgium’s two-time world champion Emma Plasschaert finished second with 28 points, while Denmark’s Anna Munch took third with 34. Rose became the first non-European to win the title in 20 years, following China’s Xu Lijia in 2006. The ILCA 6 is the women’s single-handed dinghy class used in Olympic competition.

Rose celebrated by deliberately capsizing her boat and jumping into the water after the result was confirmed. Her consistency proved decisive in a final contested by 10 boats, where changing conditions placed a premium on minimizing poor finishes. The championship adds a major global title for U.S. sailing and gives Rose a benchmark result in one of the sport’s most competitive individual classes.
dek: The American sailor finished with 23 points to become the first non-European women’s champion in the Olympic dinghy class since 2006.
headline: Charlotte Rose wins ILCA 6 world title in Dublin Bay
